results.title: Cheong Wa Dae says US midterm results unlikely to affect Korea-US alliance
results.content: Cheong Wa Dae said Thursday it does not expect the results of the U.S. midterm elections to affect bilateral alliance, vowing to continue efforts to further develop the decadeslong alliance. "The Korea-U.S. alliance is one that has developed solidly over more than 70 years based on bipartisan U.S. support, and the results of certain elections are unlikely to affect the alliance," presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung told a press briefing following a meeting presided by President Lee Jae Myung. Kang said the Korean government would closely communicate and cooperate with both the U.S. administration and Congress to pursue the development of the alliance, while monitoring any changes in the political landscape. Kang, however, said the U.S. midterm elections were not discussed during Thursday's meeting. She added that Seoul will continue to pursue investment projects in the U.S. based on i

results.title: UNCHILD returns as quirky heroes with 'TiNG TiNG'
results.content: K-pop girl group UNCHILD returned Thursday as “bug busters,” unveiling its second digital single, “TiNG TiNG,” with a playful mission to take on digital glitches. During a media showcase at NOL Theater Hapjeong in Seoul, five members — Yeeun, Tina, Ako, Evon, Haeun — introduced a release that turns their unconventional identity into a colorful superhero adventure. Taking a playful cue from “Ghostbusters,” the concept casts the members as offbeat heroes pairing house music with playful characters and choreography incorporating locking. “If our debut showcase was about introducing UNCHILD, this is about showing a new side of ourselves, so we feel nervous,” Yeeun said. The six-member group debuted in April under High Up Entertainment, becoming the agency’s first new girl group since STAYC. results.title: N. Korean fishing boat found in waters off Ulleungdo
results.content: A North Korean fishing boat was found in international waters north of eastern Ulleung Island and is currently being probed, South Korean military said Thursday. According to the military, the fishing boat was detected on Tuesday in international waters. But it did not provide further details, including how many crew were aboard or whether they wished to defect or return to the North.

results.title: Sewol ferry sinking archive, ancient cookbooks added to regional UNESCO list
results.content: An archive documenting the 2014 Sewol ferry sinking and ancient Korean cookbooks have been added to a regional list of the UNESCO Memory of the World program Thursday. The "Danwon High School 4.16 Archive: Records of Citizens' Memory and Healing Movements" was granted inscription at a general meeting of the UNESCO Memory of the World Committee for Asia and the Pacific held in Jakarta. The "Suunjapbang and Eumsikdimibang: Community Archives of Traditional Korean Culinary Knowledge," another submission by South Korea, also made the list. The Sewol archive comprises 235,220 pieces of records related to the maritime disaster on April 16, 2014, when the ferry sank en route to the southern resort island of Jeju, killing 304 passengers. Danwon High School in Ansan, Gyeonggi Province, suffered one of the biggest casualties, with 250 of 325 students who were aboard the ferry for a school trip kil

results.title: Court rejects injunction lawsuit by Coupang over data breach-related fine
results.content: A Seoul court Thursday rejected an injunction lawsuit by e-commerce firm Coupang filed against a fine of some 423 billion won ($315 million) levied by a state-run data protection agency over its massive data leak. The Seoul Administrative Court said there is no need to nullify the fine imposed by the Personal Information Protection Commission in June this year over privacy violations, including a massive data breach that affected more than 37 million users. It marked the largest fine ever imposed by the regulator on a single company, according to the commission. The punitive measures came more than six months after Coupang belatedly reported a large-scale data breach last November of personal information of users in South Korea, including their names, phone numbers and delivery details. results.title: Appeals court to rule on ex-President Yoon's martial law case on Jan. 26
results.content: An appeals court said Thursday it will deliver its verdict in January next year on former President Yoon Suk Yeol's insurrection charges stemming from his martial law declaration. The sentencing hearing will be held Jan. 26, the bench overseeing his appeal at the Seoul High Court said. A district court sentenced Yoon to life in prison in February, after finding him guilty of leading an insurrection through the martial law bid on Dec. 3, 2024, with the stated aim of eradicating "anti-state forces." Earlier, special counsel Cho Eun-suk's team again sought the death penalty for Yoon. The team also sought life imprisonment for former Defense Minister Kim Yong-hyun and a 30-year prison term for former Defense Intelligence Commander Noh Sang-won for their roles in the martial law bid. results.title: China's top diplomat meets visiting NK party secretary
results.content: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Thursday met a senior North Korean ruling party official and his delegation in Beijing, and reiterated China's commitment to cementing bilateral relations, according to his party. Wang held the talks with Kim Song-nam, a member of the Political Bureau of the Workers' Party of Korea and a party secretary, according to a post on the official WeChat account of the International Department of the Communist Party of China's central committee. Kim's delegation arrived in Beijing on Tuesday as China and the North are seeking to reinforce their cooperation after bilateral relations apparently weakened amid deepening alignment between Moscow and Pyongyang over the war in Ukraine. results.title: 'Itaewon Class' to get Thai adaptation
results.content: Two Korean webtoons, "Itaewon Class" and "The Spooky Love Tale of Gongchan Seol," are set to be adapted into Thai television dramas, extending the international reach of Korean webtoon-based productions. "Itaewon Class," which has already been adapted for television in Korea, Japan and Taiwan, will expand into Thailand, while "The Spooky Love Tale of Gongchan Seol" will be reimagined as a horror romance series for local audiences. Kakao Entertainment said Thursday that both titles were included in the drama lineup unveiled Tuesday at GMMTVNEXT: GENERATION HAPPY, a production presentation hosted by Thai entertainment company GMMTV. The main cast members were also announced at the event. GMMTV operates across television dramas, films, variety shows and artist management. results.content: Korea is notorious for its long and grueling work hours, the pressures of "hoesik" — a workplace dinner gathering that usually involves alcohol consumption — and the omnipresent crowds of uncaring people that always seem to go slightly too slow on the way to the subway escalators. While many of these aspects have improved over the years, the way home from work still remains an exhausting experience for many. For those who wish to spend their time after work productively, switching to the right state of mind during the commute — often with a relatable or cathartic song — is an essential step in retaining the energy to last into the evening hours. results.title: KT&G posts record Q3 earnings, unveils $3.7 bil. shareholder return plan
results.content: KT&G posted record quarterly revenue and operating profit in the third quarter, driven by growth across its core businesses, while unveiling a four-year shareholder return plan worth 5 trillion won ($3.7 billion). The tobacco and consumer goods company said Thursday that consolidated revenue rose 4.3 percent from a year earlier to 1.91 trillion won, while operating profit increased 13.9 percent to 530.1 billion won. Both figures marked quarterly records. Its cigarette business generated record revenue of 1.31 trillion won, up 6 percent, and operating profit of 425.5 billion won, up 14.4 percent. Its operating margin improved 2.4 percentage points to 32.6 percent. The global cigarette business marked its 10th consecutive quarter of growth in sales volume, revenue and operating profit. results.title: Special counsel seeks 1-yr prison term for CIO chief for dereliction of duty
results.content: A special counsel team on Thursday sought a one-year prison term for the head of the anti-graft agency on charges of dereliction of duty over a criminal complaint filed against one of his subordinates. Special counsel Lee Myeong-hyeon's team requested the sentence for Oh Dong-woon, chief prosecutor of the Corruption Investigation Office for High-ranking Officials (CIO), during his trial's final hearing at the Seoul Central District Court. Oh is accused of attempting to bury an investigation into Song Chang-jin, a former senior CIO prosecutor, who had become subject to a criminal complaint filed by then opposition Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) lawmakers in August 2024. Oh allegedly failed to transfer the complaint to the Supreme Prosecutors Office, as required by law, for 11 months. The special counsel team believes Oh knowingly tried to obstruct an investigation into Song. DPK lawmaker

results.title: Samsung retains top spots in global DRAM market in Q3
results.content: Korean chip giant Samsung Electronics maintained its top position in the global DRAM market in the third quarter, followed by its domestic rival SK hynix, industry data showed Thursday. Samsung Electronics accounted for 38 percent of the global DRAM market by revenue in the July-September period, down slightly from 39 percent three months earlier, according to market tracker Counterpoint Research. SK hynix regained some of the market share it had lost earlier this year, with its share rising 3 percentage points from the previous quarter to 29 percent. U.S. chipmaker Micron Technology ranked third with a 21 percent share, followed by China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) at 9 percent. results.title: KOSPI tumbles as Democrat sweep fuels AI infrastructure concerns
results.content: Korean stocks plunged Thursday, as concerns over tighter U.S. regulation of artificial intelligence (AI) and data center development triggered a broad sell-off in semiconductor shares following sweeping Democratic victories in the midterm elections. The benchmark KOSPI opened at 5,580.09, down 1.82 percent from the previous close, according to the Korea Exchange. It remained in negative territory throughout the session, eventually closing at 5,383.80, down 5.28 percent. The decline was driven largely by a rout in Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, the country’s two semiconductor heavyweights, which together account for roughly half of KOSPI’s market capitalization. Their outsized weight left the index particularly vulnerable to a shift in sentiment toward the chip sector. SK hynix plunged 9.46 percent to 1.26 million won, while Samsung Electronics tumbled 7.57 percent to close at 201,500

results.title: Samsung honors 10 researchers for contributions to science, innovation
results.content: Samsung Electronics has recognized 10 researchers for their contributions to fundamental science and technological innovation, presenting awards for the first time since launching its technology research support program in 2013. The researchers were honored at Samsung Science & Technology Annual Forum 2026, held Thursday in southern Seoul. The event drew about 450 researchers and leaders from the scientific community. The 10 awardees were selected from 644 completed projects in basic science and materials and ICT, based on their research quality, potential for further development, professional growth and contributions to academia and industry. Four researchers were recognized in basic science, including Oh Sung-jin, a mathematics professor at the University of California, Berkeley, and Lee Hyun-woo, a physics professor at Pohang University of Science and Technology. results.title: Special counsel bill on alleged fabricated indictments introduced at plenary session
results.content: A bill calling for a special counsel probe into allegations of fabricated indictments targeting President Lee Jae Myung and others was brought before a plenary session of the National Assembly on Thursday. The bill was introduced by Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik over objections from the main opposition People Power Party (PPP), setting the stage for a vote led by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), which holds a majority in the Assembly. The PPP immediately launched a filibuster, but the DPK said it will end the tactic after 24 hours in accordance with relevant rules and put the bill to a vote Friday. The bill, which was first introduced by the DPK in April, calls for an independent counsel to investigate allegations the prosecution under former President Yoon Suk Yeol fabricated evidence or induced false testimonies to build cases against then opposition leader Lee and others.

results.title: 'Coupang uses US lobbying to frame Korean sanctions as discrimination'
results.content: Coupang is using its lobbying network in Washington to portray Korea’s enforcement of domestic laws as discrimination against American businesses, according to a ruling party lawmaker, who said Seoul’s sanctions on the e-commerce firm are based on the firm’s obvious misconduct, not its nationality. "Claims that Korea is discriminating against an American company are not based on the facts, and they are a narrative created by Coupang's lobbying in the United States,” Rep. Min Byoung-dug from the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) told The Korea Times during an interview on Thursday. "We must distinguish the position of Washington from the voice Coupang has bought through lobbying." He argued that allegations of anti-U.S. bias distort Korea’s enforcement record and risk turning a domestic competition law dispute into a bilateral trade issue. results.title: Korea seeks another crypto tax delay over gaps in overseas data and rules
results.content: The government will seek to postpone cryptocurrency income taxation by another two years to 2029, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said Thursday, renewing debate over tax fairness and policy credibility after three previous postponements. Lee said more time is needed to secure overseas transaction data and refine the rules. But the reversal, just a month after the government reiterated its commitment to proceeding in January, has drawn criticism over policy predictability and possible political motivations. At a briefing, Lee said the government would work with the National Assembly to pursue the delay. The announcement came a day after ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) Chairman Kim Min-seok formally requested another postponement. results.title: Seoul gears up to welcome 1 mil. pilgrims for 2027 World Youth Day
results.content: Up to 1 million people are expected to gather in Seoul for the closing mass of the 2027 World Youth Day (WYD), marking a historic moment as the global Catholic youth festival is held for the first time in a country where Christians do not hold a majority in the population. The WYD Seoul 2027 event, running from Aug. 3 to 8, 2027, will bring an estimated 400,000 international pilgrims from around 190 countries together with 100,000 domestic participants, the organizing committee said, Thursday. Sharing its detailed roadmap for the international event, Archbishop Peter Chung Soon-taick of the Archdiocese of Seoul emphasized the deeper meaning of the gathering, pointing to the isolation faced by younger generations in the digital age. results.title: 3-year prison term finalized for ex-PSS chief for obstructing Yoon's arrest
results.content: A three-year prison term was finalized Thursday for a former chief of the Presidential Security Service (PSS) for blocking investigators from executing a warrant to detain former President Yoon Suk Yeol last year, according to legal sources. Last week, the Seoul High Court handed down the verdict. Both Park and prosecutors had seven days to appeal the decision to the Supreme Court, but neither side filed an appeal by the Wednesday deadline, resulting in the finalization of the sentence, the sources said. Park and other former PSS officials were indicted for obstructing investigators' attempts to execute an arrest warrant for Yoon at the presidential residence in January 2025 over his imposition of martial law. results.title: Lee calls for virtuous cycle to translate exports growth into domestic demand recovery
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday instructed officials to help build an economic virtuous cycle in which Korea's recent export growth can translate into a recovery in domestic demand, leading to the development of both large conglomerates and smaller firms. Lee issued the instruction at a meeting with his key aides amid strong economic indicators driven by brisk exports. His remarks came shortly after the Bank of Korea reported that the country posted an all-time high current account surplus of over $60 billion in September, buoyed by strong semiconductor exports. Earlier data also showed that Korea's exports jumped 93.7 percent from a year earlier to $115.3 billion in October, the second-highest monthly figure in the country's history following the $121.1 billion posted just a month before. results.title: FM Cho to attend G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris next week
results.content: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun will visit Paris next week to attend the Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers' meeting, the foreign ministry said Thursday. This year's second G7 ministerial meeting, scheduled for Monday to Tuesday in Marseille, is expected to address key global challenges, including artificial intelligence (AI) and developments in the Middle East, following the G7 leaders' summit in June, according to the ministry. Korea will attend the meeting at the invitation of France, which holds the G7 presidency, following its participation in the first ministerial meeting in March. "The participation is aimed at strengthening our partnership with G7 members and enhancing our standing as a globally responsible country," ministry spokesperson Park Doo-soon told a press briefing. results.title: N. Korea signals openness to dialogue if talks serve its interests: unification minister
results.content: North Korea is signaling that it is open to dialogue with the United States if such talks serve its interests, Unification Minister Chung Dong-young said Thursday, a day after the sister of the North's leader Kim Jong-un said dialogue with Washington remains among potential options for peace. Chung offered the assessment during a parliamentary interpellation session as Seoul seeks to resume diplomacy with Pyongyang to ease cross-border tension and improve inter-Korean relations. "(North Korea) is sending a signal that possibilities of dialogue remain open if talks serve its interests," the minister said. "Yesterday, (the North) said directly that it understands dialogue is necessary for peace." results.title: Korea reassesses trade, security ties after Democrats sweep US Congress
results.content: Seoul is assessing the fallout from the Democrats’ sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections, Tuesday, preparing for possible changes in trade, security and nuclear cooperation while seeking to keep existing agreements with Washington on track. "The government will analyze changes in the U.S. political landscape following the midterm elections and continue to communicate and cooperate closely with the U.S. administration and Congress," presidential chief spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said during a press briefing, Thursday. results.title: Trump must heed US voters' message
results.content: The results of the U.S. midterm elections arrived earlier than expected here in Korea, and with a definitive outcome. The Democrats won control of Congress, seizing both the House and the Senate. The forecast for a "blue wave" changed to a "blue tsunami" in a matter of hours, according to U.S. reports, as voters signaled they wanted change. The Democrats' victory was widely viewed as a repudiation of U.S. President Donald Trump's nearly two years in office. South Koreans closely watched the race for the Senate, where the decisive powers to check presidential powers lay. Democratic candidates even won Senate races in the traditionally Republican states of Texas, Kansas and North and South Carolina. results.title: S. Korea joins as co-sponsor of UN resolution on N. Korean human rights
results.content: South Korea has decided to co-sponsor this year's U.N. General Assembly resolution on North Korean human rights, which calls for an end to human rights violations in the reclusive country while stressing the importance of dialogue with Pyongyang, the foreign ministry said Thursday. The resolution, proposed by the European Union (EU), is currently under review by the Third Committee of the U.N. General Assembly in New York and is expected to be adopted by the committee around Nov. 18-19. "As it is crucial to make practical improvements in the human rights of North Korean residents, the government has joined as a co-sponsor of this year's resolution as part of its efforts to continue international cooperation," the ministry said in a press release. results.title: Financial policymakers to monitor US AI, trade policies following election
results.content: Korea's key financial policymakers on Thursday vowed to closely monitor potential changes in U.S. policies on artificial intelligence (AI) and trade and their implications for the Korean economy. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il discussed the issues with Bank of Korea (BOK) Gov. Shin Hyun-song, Financial Services Commission Chairman Lee Eog-weon and Financial Supervisory Service Gov. Lee Chan-jin after the U.S. Democratic Party secured a huge win in the midterm elections this week. During the meeting, the officials noted that despite gains in major stock markets in the United States and Europe, concerns over tighter regulation of the AI industry had led to declines in semiconductor shares. results.title: From prince to emperor: Ju Ji-hoon's appearance in 'The Remarried Empress' sparks debate
results.content: Nearly 20 years after winning hearts as a young crown prince in the hit Korean drama "Princess Hours," actor Ju Ji-hoon has returned to a royal role in Disney+'s "The Remarried Empress." But his transformation into an emperor is drawing mixed reactions, with some viewers questioning his on-screen appearance and styling while others praise his commanding performance. "The Remarried Empress," which premiered on Disney+ on Nov. 3, is based on the popular Korean web novel and webtoon of the same name. The adaptation had attracted considerable attention from fans of the original story even before its release. Following the premiere, Ju's appearance as Sovieshu, the emperor of the Eastern Empire, quickly became a talking point among viewers. results.title: No talks yet on sanctions over N. Korea's alleged Binance theft: unification ministry
results.content: The government has not begun discussing sanctions on North Korea over its alleged theft of a massive amount of cryptocurrency, a unification ministry official said Thursday. "As of now, the government has not fully grasped the exact circumstances of the hacking case, so a discussion on how to respond to it has not even begun," the official told reporters at the government complex in Seoul. "Internal sharing and discussion inside the government are needed, but we have not reached that stage," the official added. Last week, the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said North Korea was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. results.title: Atomy tops Asia's best workplace list with human-centered management
results.content: Korean direct marketing company Atomy ranked first in the small and medium-sized business category of Great Place to Work's (GPTW) 2026 Best Workplaces in Asia list, recognition that the company attributes to its management philosophy centered on employee trust and autonomy. The global network marketing company, which now operates in 27 countries, said it was the first Korean company to top the category, moving up from third place last year. The latest assessment covered its operations in Korea, China, the Philippines, Cambodia and Indonesia, up from three countries in the previous evaluation. The ranking is based on employees' assessments of their workplaces, covering trust in management, respect, fairness, pride and camaraderie. results.title: Korea tightens corporate governance disclosure rules to strengthen shareholder protections
results.content: All companies listed on the benchmark KOSPI will face tougher disclosure requirements on boardroom changes and major corporate transactions under new rules designed to give shareholders greater oversight of corporate governance, financial authorities said Thursday. The changes, announced by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Exchange, expand the information companies must provide in their annual corporate governance reports. The move comes after the reporting requirement was extended to all 826 KOSPI-listed companies this year. One focus is on preventing companies from circumventing the revised Commercial Act that is designed to give minority shareholders a greater say in board appointments.
